A cleanup-only-on-normal-return countermodel passes both observations but leaks on timeout and SystemExit; section 5 explicitly promises both exceptional paths. Q05 tests only ls-remote/7a failure. Q06 tests a measured blob mismatch and Q08 a measured CRLF match; no row makes the 7b hash/blob measurement fail. This is a source/table coverage observation, not a measured production bypass.

findings.claim: H1 does not freeze the distinction between structural reduction eligibility and a switch-gated CI decision. Plan r4 requires chuan-bi to pass vars into the classifier and missing/unknown permission to yield chay. B4 removes every such permission input, yet expects the same entry point to emit bo_qua/dich before it reads the live switch. A producer implementing the stated CI fail-closed rule can therefore make beta unreachable, even with the correct live switch. The constant-output beta/delta fixtures conceal this integration ambiguity.

evidence.command: python3 -B /tmp/wp1462-r4-evidence/probe_contract_gaps.py; inspect ops/ci_duong_nhanh.py:794-827 and plan r4 A+1
observed: The current producer prints its decision and writes the same decision to GITHUB_OUTPUT; it has no frozen separate eligibility interface. PR3/PR6 do not exist yet, so this is a specification integration counterexample, not a claim of a current production bug.

A stand-in producer following the plan rule emits cong_cu=bo_qua with the correct permission in its CI environment. Under B4 section 5’s fresh allowlisted environment, the same entry point emits cong_cu=chay with rc=0. The written H1 mapping yields khong_giam; section 4 rejects before GET, even though the live switch is stipulated correct.

The same dependency applies to g5_che_do=dich for PR6. H1 states names/framing but never says which outputs are raw eligibility and which are permission-filtered, nor how one entry point satisfies both consumers. GT-5/GT-7 use fixtures that print bo_qua/dich unconditionally, so the required tests do not resolve the producer contract.

suggested_fix.where: H1 producer/consumer contract, PR3/PR6 obligations, integration fixtures and any associated plan deviation.
suggested_fix.how: Freeze an explicit separation: for example, trusted stdout eligibility independent of switch state, with separately permission-gated CI exports. Specify both consumers and the fail-closed behavior when permission is absent; record any necessary plan interpretation/deviation for owner approval. Keep authorization in B4’s subsequent live GET and keep caller-controlled inputs unable to grant a reduction.
suggested_fix.test: Use a producer fixture implementing both eligibility and CI permission filtering. On the same eligible diff, missing/invalid CI permission must export the full CI decision; the trusted B4 call must still identify eligibility, then accept only a correct live switch. Exercise both bo_moi and che_do_dich and all switch states.
suggested_fix.may_spawn: An H1 revision and corresponding obligations in PR3/PR6. B4 must not edit their out-of-scope classifier/workflow files or reintroduce CI-log fallback, cached permission, or a caller-controlled allow switch.

notes: Round 4: three open P2 cause classes; no separate P0/P1 findings. The group-G wording manifestation is P3 within B4-S05. Slugs are assigned here to all 12 inherited finding IDs, preserving their original causes and source SHAs; no class is merged or renamed to reset history. Of the three classes open after round 3, only B4-S12 is fully closed at specification level: 1/3. B4-S05 and B4-S10 remain partial; B4-S13 is new and outside that denominator. B4-S05 has now appeared in four reviews and S10 in three: preserve the protocol section 12 checkpoint/history and r86 call counters; this report grants no new remediation calls. No removed authorization store, global FULL, CI-log fallback, updated_at predicate or pull_request_target mechanism was found reintroduced. D-6 still requires the future explicit owner/Mission disposition already required by the candidate. Model/provider identity: openai_codex, family openai, execution_surface codex_cli (shell/tool runtime), transport machine; exact served model/effort and launcher/service identity attestation KHONG_DO_DUOC. No cross_approved, human audit, execution lease or land authority is claimed. Runtime Linux/Python 3.13.18/Git 2.43.0; workspace-write sandbox with assigned Git metadata read-only. Scratch and disposable fixture repositories are under /tmp/wp1462-r4-evidence and /tmp/wp1462-r4-fetch; the assigned checkout was not edited. Endpoint equality does not attest every intermediate filesystem state or the source mirror’s contents. Upstream all-ref freshness and live owner budget counters were not independently measured; current master/candidate were checked by GitHub reads. All DA_VA_THAT labels mean the prior specification defect is closed, not that future implementation or CI acceptance passed. Final output validation initially used an overbroad assertion that ignored paths must be absent; it failed on the pre-existing .codex/ directory. Comparing against the recorded initial inventory confirms no path delta. This validation error was corrected; no repository file was changed or removed.
